notes: These examples describe reusable candidate shapes, not qrel labels or Brian-reviewed promotion decisions.

examples.description: A company or brand domain appears across multiple source surfaces with an entity-like name.
A plausible company domain appears, but the observed page title is a listicle, comparison, or source article.
A publisher, directory, or comparison page describes the market and should not become a company profile.
A source domain appears as evidence but is not itself the discovered market actor.
A plausible brand name is extracted from a source page but lacks a verified domain.
A product or workflow target may be relevant, but it is not automatically a company-profile target.
Navigation labels, login pages, utility hosts, and malformed artifacts should not enter capture.
The evidence suggests a possible entity, but kind or capture-worthiness is ambiguous.
